title: Top Laptops for Video Editing & Creators (2026)
summary: MacBooks lead most video-editing roundups, with the ROG Zephyrus as the Windows alternative that comes up most often.
method: Picks come from BestReviews, Digit, UDN's laptop review blog and two smaller testing roundups. Only models or lines named by at least two of these sources are listed. Several sources are small review blogs, so treat the details as a starting point.
assumptions: We show no prices because laptop prices change often. Sources agree that editors need plenty of RAM, fast storage and a strong GPU or chip, so check memory and storage before you buy.

products.name: Apple MacBook Pro (M5 / M5 Pro)
why: BestReviews makes the MacBook Pro with the M5 Pro chip its best of the best for photo and video editing. Digit says that if you aren't interested in a gaming laptop, the latest MacBook Pro is the first name that comes to mind, and notes the older M4 chip still edits videos well.
Smaller review roundups also place the 14-inch MacBook Pro first for editors.
pros: Works with Final Cut Pro, Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve
Long battery life for a powerful laptop
products.skip_if: You mostly cut 1080p and want to save money

products.name: Apple MacBook Air 15-inch (M4 / M5)
why: BestReviews names the 15-inch MacBook Air with the M4 chip its pick for most people, powerful enough for general photo and video work, and also calls the M5 version best bang for the buck.
Another roundup makes the 13-inch M5 Air its editor's choice for portability but warns the 512GB base storage fills up fast for video.
cons: Less sustained power than a MacBook Pro
Base storage fills up quickly with video
products.skip_if: You edit heavy multicam or 8K projects

products.name: ASUS ROG Zephyrus G14 / G15
why: UDN's laptop blog calls the ROG Zephyrus G15 a mid-range gaming laptop that is also great for 4K video editing, and notes its 90Wh battery lasts about 5 hours of regular use.
Another testing roundup picks the ROG Zephyrus G14 (2025) as the best Windows laptop for video editing.
pros: Dedicated graphics for editing and games
cons: Battery lasts only about 5 hours under regular use (UDN)
products.best_for: Editors who want Windows and a dedicated GPU, plus some gaming
products.skip_if: You edit on battery a lot
